vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: comic-script
Version: 2.3.4

The skill bundle provides utility scripts for comic script writing and general content creation. The scripts (comic.sh and script.sh) are simple text-processing tools that generate templates and tips; they do not perform network requests, access sensitive files, or execute untrusted code. While there are minor inconsistencies between the documentation in SKILL.md and the actual script commands, no malicious intent or high-risk behaviors were identified.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions are coherent with a comic/script-writing helper: it runs local scripts, writes small logs to a user data directory, does not request credentials, and contains no network or exfiltration behavior.

dimensions.detail: Name/description describe a comic storyboard/script writer; the included scripts implement storyboard, character, dialogue, layout templates and a general content-helper CLI. The requested resources (none) are consistent with this purpose. The only mild mismatch is that scripts/script.sh also offers generic content/SEO commands beyond strictly 'comic' features, but this is plausible for a content creation tool.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md is a concise CLI-oriented instruction set. The runtime scripts operate locally and only read their arguments and environment vars (COMIC_SCRIPT_DIR/XDG_DATA_HOME/HOME). They do not reference or attempt to read system credentials, unrelated config paths, or network endpoints. They do write usage/history logs to a per-user data directory, which is consistent with a CLI assistant.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install specification (instruction-only at registry level). The repository includes shell scripts embedded with a short Python snippet; nothing downloads remote artifacts or extracts archives. No high-risk install behavior detected.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not require secrets or credentials. It honors COMIC_SCRIPT_DIR/XDG_DATA_HOME (falling back to $HOME/.local/share/comic-script) and creates a history.log in that directory. Writing to a per-user data directory is reasonable for this tool, but users should be aware of persistent local storage of command history/log entries.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Flags show always:false and normal autonomous-invocation defaults. The skill does not request elevated privileges or modify other skills or system-wide configs. Its persistence is limited to creating a data directory and log files under the user's home.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: local scripts generate comic/story templates and small logs. Before installing, note that it will create a data directory (by default $HOME/.local/share/comic-script) and append to history.log. If you prefer no persistent files, set COMIC_SCRIPT_DIR to a temporary location or inspect/modify the scripts. There are no network calls or credential requests in the provided files, but if the published skill in the registry later adds an install step or remote download, re-check for unexpected URLs or extraction. If you want extra caution, run the scripts inside a sandbox or container and review the two shell files for any future changes.
